```{r load library, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(gridExtra)
library(reshape2)
library(here)
library(knitr)
```

```{r yeses, include=FALSE}
options(scipen=999)
source(here("ext", "get_betas.R"))
source(here("ext", "get_treatment_counts.R"))
source(here("ext", "get_pvalues.R"))

#the dataset used for paper 
#Neuroethics_Judgement <- read.csv(here::here("data", "Cleaned_Pilot", "clean_data_longV2.csv"), stringsAsFactors=TRUE)


read.csv(here("data", "Cleaned_Pilot", "Post_hoc_risk_test_all_batches.csv"), header=TRUE, comment.char="#", stringsAsFactors=TRUE) %>% 
  filter(batch == 1 | batch == 2 | batch == 3 | batch == 4) -> batch.total

N <- batch.total %>%
  select(user_id, batch) %>% 
  group_by(user_id, batch) %>% 
  summarize(n = n())
N$batch <- as.factor(N$batch)
summary(N$batch)
```
Batch 1 is our two samples of data gathered prior to the 70 cut off **(59 subjects)**

Batch 2 is our first data set post the 70 cut off **(28 subjects)**

Batch 3 is our first data set post deployment **(45 subjects)**

Batch total contains a total of **132 subjects**

```{r calculate betas}
batch.total %>% 
  dplyr::select(user_id, risk, gain, no_effect, experimental_treatment_selected, batch) %>%
  group_by(user_id) %>% #group by user id
  mutate(risk.c = scale(risk, scale = F)) %>% #mean center variables
  mutate(gain.c = scale(gain, scale = F)) %>% 
  mutate(treatment = ifelse(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment", 1, 0)) -> logit.data 

get_betas(logit.data,treatment ~ risk.c + gain.c) -> data #this takes the data and the formula

colnames(data) <-  c("user_id", "risk", "gain", "no_effect", "experimental_treatment_selected", 
"batch", "risk.centered", "gain.centered", "treatment", "(Intercept)", "Risk_Beta", 
"Gain_Beta", "risk_vif", "gain_vif", "vif", "null.deviance", 
"df.null", "logLik", "AIC", "BIC", "deviance", "df.residual", 
"nobs")

get_pvalues(logit.data, treatment ~ risk.c + gain.c) -> pvalues

data <- merge(data, pvalues, "user_id")
#100% risk of harm 
data %>% 
    filter(batch == 1 | batch == 2) %>% 
    filter(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment") -> batch.1
#first batch with 70%
data %>% 
    filter(batch == 3) %>% 
    filter(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment") -> batch.2
#Study 1st deployment batch
data %>% 
    filter(batch == 4) %>% 
    filter(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment") -> batch.3

```

For batch one, how many people said Yes above 75? 
```{r}
batch.1 %>% 
  select(user_id, risk) %>% 
  filter(risk > 70) %>% 
  group_by(user_id) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = n)) + geom_histogram(bins =10)

batch.3 %>% 
  select(user_id, risk) %>% 
  filter(risk > 65) %>% 
  group_by(user_id) %>% 
  count() 

data %>% 
    filter(batch == 4) %>% 
  select(user_id, risk, experimental_treatment_selected) %>% 
  filter(risk > 40) %>% 
  group_by(user_id, experimental_treatment_selected) %>% 
  count() 

 data %>% 
    filter(batch == 4) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x=risk, color=user_id)) + geom_density()+
  theme(legend.position="none")+
   facet_wrap(~experimental_treatment_selected, nrow = 2)

```

```{r pvalues, fig.height=5, fig.width=16, dpi=300, echo=FALSE}

dat.2 = distinct(select(batch.2, user_id, Risk_sig, Gain_sig))
dat.3 = distinct(select(batch.3, user_id, Risk_sig, Gain_sig))

dat.1 <- melt(dat.1, 
                       id = c("user_id"),
                       variable.name = "type", 
                       value.name = "sig")

dat.2 <- melt(dat.2, 
                       id = c("user_id"),
                       variable.name = "type", 
                       value.name = "sig")

dat.3 <- melt(dat.3, 
                       id = c("user_id"),
                       variable.name = "type", 
                       value.name = "sig")

#Significant plots
p1 <- ggplot(dat.1, aes(x = type, fill = as.factor(sig))) +
         geom_bar(color = 'black', stat="count", position = "dodge")+
         scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 110))+ggtitle("Batch 1") +theme(plot.title = element_text(lineheight=.8, face="bold"))

p2 <- ggplot(dat.2, aes(x = type, fill = as.factor(sig))) +
         geom_bar(color = 'black', stat="count", position = "dodge")+
         scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 110))+ggtitle("Batch 2") +theme(plot.title = element_text(lineheight=.8, face="bold"))

p3 <- ggplot(dat.3, aes(x = type, fill = as.factor(sig))) +
         geom_bar(color = 'black', stat="count", position = "dodge")+
         scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 110))+ggtitle("Batch 3") +theme(plot.title = element_text(lineheight=.8, face="bold"))

grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, ncol = 3)
```

Upon piloting, we identified `r ` \% who had no statistically significant risk/benefit responsiveness. Among those with risk-responsiveness, risk had a diminishing effect by 70 \% risk. 

```{r}
batch.1 %>% 
  dplyr::select(user_id,Risk_sig, Gain_sig) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  filter(Risk_sig == "Not Significant") %>% 
  count()

24/55
```


We determined that risk had a negligible effect above 70\%. We design the trials to max 70 because it increased the frequency of "yes" responses, allowing us to obtain more reliable risk beta coefficients. In addition, this strategy still allowed us to identify participants who had no statistically significant risk response, because in the pilot data, flat responders were flat through the entire range of risks. 

We executed one more pilot with risks capped at 70\%, finding that we still observed that participants stopped endorsing treatments at risk levels below 70\%, and X participants exhibited evidence of ceiling effects at 70\% in piloting. Thus, the final task design used up to a 90\% chance of benefits and 70\% chance of risks, and we were able to model the independent effect of each variable in the current study.
